$comment: Source for skills/prompt-engine/references/media-targets.md (generated by scripts/build.mjs). status: verified = a primary source was opened; secondary = official docs seen only through search snippets; unverified = not confirmed. Recheck entries older than 60 days.

targets.name: Midjourney
targets.prompt_style: Short descriptive prose, with parameters at the very end after a space. Short, simple prompts usually work best; use exact numbers ("three cats", not "cats").
targets.exclusions: --no item, one word per item: multi-word phrases are read word by word. Writing "no cake" in the prompt text can still produce cake.
targets.settings: Inline parameters at the end, with no commas inside them: --ar W:H (whole numbers), --stylize, --chaos, --raw. Video: --motion low|high, --loop.
targets.references: --sref for style. Image and character reference features have changed between versions, so ask which version the user is on or label it as an assumption.
targets.text: Exact words in double quotes; short words work best.

targets.name: OpenAI GPT Image (also image generation in ChatGPT)
targets.prompt_style: A descriptive paragraph, or short labeled lines for complex requests: scene or background, then subject, then key details, then constraints. Say what the image is for (ad, UI mock, infographic).
targets.exclusions: Plain constraints in the prompt work, such as "no watermark, no extra text".
targets.settings: API parameters, not prose: size, quality, background (transparent needs PNG or WebP output), output_format, n.
targets.references: Refer to input images by index ("Image 1", "Image 2"). For edits: "Change only X; keep everything else the same", repeating the keep list each turn.
targets.text: Put exact text in quotes and describe font, placement and size; spell unusual words letter by letter.

targets.name: Google Gemini image models ("Nano Banana")
targets.prompt_style: A narrative paragraph, not a keyword list: subject, action, location or context, composition, style. With reference images, say how they relate to the new scene.
targets.exclusions: Describe what you want instead of what you don't ("an empty street", not "no cars").
targets.settings: Aspect ratio and resolution are request settings.
targets.references: Name each reference's role ("use the attached photo as the character reference").
targets.text: Put exact text in quotes and say where it goes.

targets.name: FLUX (Black Forest Labs)
targets.prompt_style: Prose with the most important elements first: subject, action or pose, style or medium, setting, lighting, camera. About 30–80 words. JSON can be used to draft and is then flattened to prose.
targets.exclusions: No negative prompts: describe the result you want instead.
targets.references: Input images are passed as API parameters.
targets.text: Exact text in quotes; colors can be given as hex codes.

targets.name: Stable Diffusion (AUTOMATIC1111, ComfyUI and similar)
targets.prompt_style: Comma-separated tags, with weights for emphasis: (term:1.2). BREAK (uppercase) starts a new chunk.
targets.settings: UI or API settings (steps, sampler, size, CFG).
targets.references: Depends on the interface and extensions.
targets.text: Unreliable; plan to add text afterwards.
targets.notes: Square brackets reduce emphasis, so leave [[placeholders]] out of the prompt itself and ask for the value instead.

targets.name: Google Veo
targets.prompt_style: A paragraph in the order camera, subject, action, context, style and mood; for several moments, timestamped segments such as [00:00-00:02]. Dialogue goes in quotes; sound effects start with "SFX:" and background sound with "Ambient noise:".
targets.exclusions: A separate negative prompt field, written as a list of things to leave out.
targets.settings: Request settings: aspect ratio, duration, resolution.
targets.references: Reference images and first/last frames are request inputs.
targets.text: Avoid on-screen text; add titles and subtitles in editing.
targets.notes: Which Veo versions are available, and where, changed in 2026; check the current docs.

targets.name: Google Gemini Omni (video)
targets.prompt_style: A paragraph or timed segments. It may cut between several shots by default, so ask explicitly for "a single continuous shot, no scene cuts" when you want one take.
targets.exclusions: Short plain instructions, such as "no dialogue".
targets.references: Image roles are set with tags such as <FIRST_FRAME>, <LAST_FRAME> and <IMAGE_REF_N>; check the current docs for exact placement.
targets.text: Avoid on-screen text; add it in editing.

targets.name: Runway
targets.prompt_style: Natural language, roughly camera, then subject and action, then environment. Image-to-video: describe only the motion and call the subject "the subject".
targets.exclusions: Negative phrasing isn't supported and may backfire: write "locked camera" rather than "no camera movement".
targets.settings: UI or API settings, including duration.
targets.text: Avoid on-screen text; add it in editing.

targets.name: Kling
targets.prompt_style: Subject, movement, scene, then camera, lighting and atmosphere; timed blocks for several moments. References are named in the prompt, for example "@Image1 as the first frame".
targets.exclusions: A separate negative prompt field; keep it short (for example subtitles, background music).
targets.settings: API or app settings, including duration.
targets.text: Avoid on-screen text; add it in editing.

targets.name: Luma (Ray models)
targets.prompt_style: Natural language in the present tense, focused on the action, with secondary motion (hair, fabric, dust) for realism. A few sentences.
targets.settings: Request settings: aspect ratio, duration, resolution.
targets.references: Keyframes and character references are request inputs.
targets.text: Avoid on-screen text; add it in editing.

targets.name: ByteDance Seedance
targets.prompt_style: Open with a one-sentence summary (subject, place, event, style, camera), then time-stamped segments, with constraints last. Give every reference a role ("Image 1 is the main character").
targets.exclusions: Positive phrasing; negative prompts may be ignored.
targets.references: "Image 1 / Video 1 / Audio 1" roles in the prompt; use one input mode per request.
targets.text: Avoid on-screen text; add it in editing.

targets.name: OpenAI Sora
targets.prompt_style: Discontinued in 2026 (app in April, API in September). If a user asks for a Sora prompt, say so and offer a prompt for another video tool. Its published guide is still a good technique reference: prose scene, then camera and mood, distinct action beats, short dialogue, background sound.
